jobs.prompt: Write tools/security-scan.mjs. Plain ESM for Node 22, no dependencies, first line "// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0", compact code, no network or process access except what is passed in (every dependency is injected). Do not edit tests. It is the scanning half of the A1 security gate (docs/plans/swarm-more-upgrades-spec.md section A1): pure functions over text. Exports: (1) shannonEntropy(text): bits per character. (2) SECRET_RULES: an array of { id, name, re } (all regexes global-free; each used with exec per line) for: aws-access-key-id (AKIA|ASIA followed by 16 upper-case letters or digits), aws-secret (aws_secret_access_key followed by = or : and a 40 character base64-like value, optionally quoted), github-token (gh[pousr]_ followed by 36 or more letters or digits), slack-token (xox[baprs]- followed by 10 or more of letters, digits, dashes), stripe-live-key ((sk|rk)_live_ followed by 20 or more letters or digits), private-key-block (-----BEGIN followed by an optional RSA, EC, DSA, OPENSSH or PGP word and PRIVATE KEY-----), google-api-key (AIza followed by 35 of letters, digits, underscore, dash), anthropic-key (sk-ant- followed by 20 or more of letters, digits, underscore, dash), openai-key (sk- followed by 32 or more letters or digits, not preceded by a letter), jwt (eyJ... . eyJ... . signature, three base64url parts of at least 10 characters), url-password (a scheme://user:password@host URL with a password of at least 6 characters that is not a placeholder such as password, changeme, example, x or ****), generic-secret (a name containing api key, apikey, secret, token or password in any case, then = or :, then a quoted value of 20 or more characters from [A-Za-z0-9/+_=.-] whose shannonEntropy is at least 3.5 and that does not contain the words example, placeholder, your, test or dummy). (3) scanSecrets(files, { allowFingerprints = [], maxBytes = 1000000 } = {}): files is [{ path, content }] (content a string or a Buffer); skip a file whose content contains a NUL byte or is larger than maxBytes; for every line and rule that matches return { rule: id, name, path, line (1-based), fingerprint } where fingerprint is the first 12 hex characters of the sha256 of the matched text (node:crypto createHash). The finding NEVER contains the matched text or any part of the line. Skip a finding whose fingerprint is in allowFingerprints and any line that contains the marker swarm-secret-allow. At most 3 findings per rule per file and 200 in all. (4) parseNpmAudit(input): input is a JSON string or object; for npm 7 and later ({ vulnerabilities: { name: { severity, via: [...] } } }) return [{ name, severity, source: 'npm' }] and for npm 6 ({ advisories: { id: { module_name, severity, title } } }) the same shape; unknown or invalid input returns []; severities lower-cased. (5) parseOsv(input): osv-scanner JSON ({ results: [{ packages: [{ package: { name }, vulnerabilities: [{ id, database_specific: { severity } }] }] }] }) to [{ name, severity (lower-cased, 'high' when missing), id, source: 'osv' }]. (6) parsePipAudit(input): pip-audit JSON ({ dependencies: [{ name, version, vulns: [{ id }] }] } or a bare array of the same) to [{ name, severity: 'high', id, source: 'pip-audit' }] (pip-audit gives no severity so every finding counts as high). (7) blockingVulns(vulns, blockSeverities = ['high', 'critical']): the vulnerabilities whose severity is in the list. (8) parseSemgrep(input): semgrep JSON ({ results: [{ check_id, path, start: { line }, extra: { severity, message } }] }) to [{ ruleId, path, line, severity (lower-cased; semgrep ERROR becomes 'high', WARNING 'medium', INFO 'low'), message (cut to 200 characters) }]. (9) licenseBlocked(expression, { allowCopyleft = false, approved = [] } = {}): true when the SPDX-like license text names GPL or AGPL (any version, not LGPL, which is allowed) and no permissive alternative exists: for an expression with OR, it is blocked only when EVERY alternative is blocked; AND or WITH keep the alternative blocked if any part is blocked; a license listed in approved (case-insensitive exact match) is never blocked; allowCopyleft true never blocks; empty or missing license text returns false (the dependency check reports unknown licenses separately).

Write tools/security-deps.mjs. Plain ESM for Node 22, no dependencies, first line "// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0", compact code, no network or process access except what is passed in (every dependency is injected). Do not edit tests. It is the dependency half of the A1 security gate: it finds NEW dependencies in a change and checks that each one is real. Exports: (1) POPULAR_PACKAGES: an array of about 40 very popular npm package names (react, lodash, express, axios, request, moment, chalk, commander, debug, webpack, typescript, jest, eslint, prettier, vue, next, tailwindcss, dotenv, uuid, cors, mongoose, jsonwebtoken, bcrypt, passport, socket.io, redux, rxjs, underscore, async, bluebird, yargs, inquirer, glob, rimraf, minimist, semver, colors, node-fetch, body-parser). (2) editDistance(a, b): Levenshtein distance. (3) newDependencies({ before, after }): before and after are objects { 'package.json': text or null, 'requirements.txt': text or null } (any file name that starts with requirements and ends with .txt is a Python file; use the keys given); return the dependencies present after but not before, as [{ ecosystem: 'npm' | 'pypi', name, spec, dev }]: from package.json read dependencies, optionalDependencies and devDependencies (dev true for devDependencies); from requirements text read each non-comment line that starts with a package name (letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, optional extras in brackets) followed by an optional version spec, lower-case the name for pypi, skip lines starting with - or containing :// . A dependency counts as new when its ecosystem and name are not in the before set. Invalid JSON counts as no dependencies. Names that are not valid for their ecosystem (npm: lower-case letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, optional @scope/ prefix) are returned with invalid: true. (4) async checkPackage(dep, { fetchImpl, now = Date.now, policy }) where policy has { minAgeDays = 30, minWeeklyDownloads = 100 }: for npm GET https://registry.npmjs.org/ plus encodeURIComponent(name) (keep the @ and encode the slash as %2f): status 404 gives { ok: false, reasons: ['not found on the registry (made-up name?)'] }; otherwise ageDays from time.created in days (rounded down), license from the latest version (dist-tags.latest then versions[latest].license, a string or an object with type), and weekly downloads from GET https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/ plus the name (field downloads); reasons: 'younger than N days' when ageDays < minAgeDays, 'only D downloads last week' when downloads < minWeeklyDownloads, 'looks like the popular package P' when the name is not in POPULAR_PACKAGES but editDistance to one of them is 1 and (ageDays < 365 or downloads < 1000), and for a dependency flagged invalid 'not a valid package name'; for pypi GET https://pypi.org/pypi/ plus name plus /json: 404 not found; age from the earliest upload_time over all releases; license from info.license or the first classifier that starts with 'License ::' (its last segment); downloads are not available (weeklyDownloads null, not a reason). Any network error or non-ok non-404 answer gives { ok: false, reasons: ['could not verify (registry unreachable)'] } (fail closed). Return { name, ecosystem, ok: reasons.length === 0, reasons, ageDays, weeklyDownloads, license }. (5) async checkPackages(deps, options): checks at most 4 at a time and returns the results in input order.

Write tools/security-gate.mjs. Plain ESM for Node 22, no dependencies, first line "// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0", compact code, no network or process access except what is passed in (every dependency is injected). Do not edit tests. It is the A1 security gate that runs in the merge queue before a batch can merge. Read docs/plans/swarm-more-upgrades-spec.md section A1 in your context. It imports from ./security-scan.mjs (SECRET_RULES, scanSecrets, parseNpmAudit, parseOsv, parsePipAudit, blockingVulns, parseSemgrep, licenseBlocked) and ./security-deps.mjs (newDependencies, checkPackages). Exports: (1) DEFAULT_POLICY = Object.freeze({ enabled: true, minAgeDays: 30, minWeeklyDownloads: 100, blockSeverities: ['high','critical'], allowCopyleft: false, approvedLicenses: [], allowedSecretFingerprints: [] }). (2) normalizePolicy(raw): merge raw over the defaults (ignore unknown keys; enabled false only when raw.enabled === false; numbers must be non-negative finite else the default; arrays must be arrays of strings else the default); returns a plain object. (3) async runSecurityGate({ changes, policy, exec, fetchImpl, now = Date.now, cwd }): changes is [{ file, bytes (Buffer or null when deleted), previous (Buffer or null when new) }] for one merge-queue batch; exec(argv, { cwd, timeoutMs }) resolves { exitCode, stdout, stderr } and never throws on a non-zero exit (a rejection or ENOENT means the tool is missing); returns { ok, blocks, tickets, warnings, skipped, checked } where every block is { check, severity, message, path?, line?, fingerprint? }. policy.enabled === false returns { ok: true, blocks: [], tickets: [], warnings: [], skipped: ['security gate disabled by policy'], checked: [] } immediately. Steps: (a) secrets: scanSecrets over the changed files with bytes not null (path = file, content = bytes), allowFingerprints from the policy; each finding is a block { check: 'secret-scan', severity: 'critical', message: 'possible <name> in <file>:<line> (fingerprint <fp>)' } with no secret text; (b) dependencies: when any changed file is package.json or a requirements text file (name starting with requirements and ending with .txt), build before and after text maps from previous and bytes (null when absent), call newDependencies, checkPackages with fetchImpl and the policy, and make a block { check: 'package-check', severity: 'high', message: '<name>: <reasons joined by "; ">' } for every result that is not ok; (c) licenses: for each result with a license, when licenseBlocked(license, { allowCopyleft: policy.allowCopyleft, approved: policy.approvedLicenses }) add a block { check: 'license-check', severity: 'high', message: '<name> is <license>: copyleft needs the owner's approval' }; a result with an unknown license adds a warning 'license unknown for <name>'; (d) vulnerabilities: only when package.json, package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json or a requirements file changed: if package-lock.json exists in the batch or cwd, run exec(['npm', 'audit', '--json'], { cwd, timeoutMs: 120000 }) and parse with parseNpmAudit; if requirements files changed try exec(['pip-audit', '-f', 'json', '-r', <file>], ...) with parsePipAudit; also try exec(['osv-scanner', '--format', 'json', '-r', '.'], ...) when present; a missing tool adds the text '<tool> not installed' to skipped; every vulnerability from blockingVulns(all, policy.blockSeverities) becomes a block { check: 'vulnerability', severity, message: '<name> has a <severity> vulnerability' }; (e) code scan: when exec(['semgrep', '--version']) works, run exec(['semgrep', '--config', 'auto', '--json', '--quiet', ...changed text file paths (at most 200)], { cwd, timeoutMs: 180000 }) and parseSemgrep; each finding with severity high or medium becomes a ticket { title: '<ruleId> in <path>:<line>', severity, path, line, message } (tickets do not block; the spec says findings become fix tickets); semgrep missing adds 'semgrep not installed' to skipped. checked lists the checks that actually ran ('secret-scan', 'package-check', 'license-check', 'vulnerability', 'code-scan'). ok is blocks.length === 0. (4) formatBlocks(gate): one short line per block for logs. (5) lessonFor(gate, { runId, date }): returns { id, date, stage: 'merge', source: 'security-gate', summary, checks (unique check names of the blocks), tags (the check names plus 'security'), blocks: [{ check, severity, path, line, fingerprint }] } and NEVER the secret text or any package version strings beyond names; summary is plain text like '3 blocks: secret-scan x2, package-check x1'. (6) async recordGate({ root, runId, jobs, gate, appendEvent, now = Date.now, fsImpl }): when gate.blocks is non-empty: write a lesson line (JSON, newline terminated) by appending to <root>/.swarm/project/security-lessons.ndjson (create the directory recursively, file mode 0o600, use fs/promises appendFile) and call appendEvent(root, { kind: 'blocker', id: 'security-' + runId + '-' + <jobs.join('+') cut to 60 characters, with characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by _>, text: 'Security gate blocked ' + jobs.join(', ') + ': ' + formatBlocks(gate) cut to 600 characters }); return { recorded: true, lessonId }; with no blocks return { recorded: false }; never throw (return { recorded: false, error } on failure).
